countries.name: Spain
countries.label: sticky down — groceries still rose
countries.blurb: Spain is the stickiest of the eleven. Grocery prices still rose, on average, in quarters when farm prices fell.
countries.pairingNote: Pooled pair-quarters within country (equal weight per quarter×category).

countries.name: United States
countries.label: sticky both ways
countries.blurb: U.S. shelf prices barely follow the farm — up or down. Farm product is only about 11 cents of the food dollar.
countries.pairingNote: Pooled pair-quarters within country (equal weight per quarter×category).

countries.name: Italy
countries.label: sticky down — groceries still rose
countries.blurb: Italian groceries still rose when farm prices fell. The shelf kept climbing after the farm eased.
countries.pairingNote: Pooled pair-quarters within country (equal weight per quarter×category).

countries.name: France
countries.label: sticky down — groceries still rose
countries.blurb: French groceries still rose when farm prices fell. Milk is one of the closer farm-to-shelf pairs.
countries.pairingNote: Pooled pair-quarters within country (equal weight per quarter×category).

countries.name: Australia
countries.label: sticky down — groceries still rose
countries.blurb: Australian groceries still rose when factory prices fell. Only bread, dairy, and meat have a paired factory series.
countries.coverage: Fewer categories paired (3 of 6); eggs, fruit, vegetables omitted (no paired PPI).
countries.pairingNote: Pooled pair-quarters within country (equal weight per quarter×category).

countries.name: Canada
countries.label: sticky down
countries.blurb: Most Canadian foods shrug when the farm moves. Fresh vegetables are the exception — they fall when farm prices fall.
countries.pairingNote: Pooled pair-quarters within country (equal weight per quarter×category).

countries.name: United Kingdom
countries.label: rises fast, sticky down
countries.blurb: UK groceries rise quickly when factory prices rise, then barely give it back. Only grain, dairy, and meat are paired.
countries.coverage: Fewer categories paired (3 of 6); eggs, fruit, vegetables omitted (no paired PPI).
countries.pairingNote: Pooled pair-quarters within country (equal weight per quarter×category).

countries.name: Japan
countries.label: sticky down
countries.blurb: Japanese groceries barely fall when farm prices fall. Fruit and vegetables have no paired producer series here.
countries.coverage: Fewer categories paired (4 of 6); fruit, vegetables omitted (no paired PPI).
countries.pairingNote: Pooled pair-quarters within country (equal weight per quarter×category).

countries.name: Germany
countries.label: almost flat when PPI falls
countries.blurb: German groceries go almost flat when farm prices fall. The shelf does not give back the rise.
countries.pairingNote: Pooled pair-quarters within country (equal weight per quarter×category).

countries.name: Poland
countries.label: falls a little when PPI falls
countries.blurb: Polish groceries fall a little when farm prices fall — more two-sided than Spain or the U.S., still incomplete.
countries.pairingNote: Pooled pair-quarters within country (equal weight per quarter×category).

countries.name: Czechia
countries.label: moves both ways
countries.blurb: Czechia is the most two-sided country in the set. Store prices do fall with farm prices, just not one-for-one.
countries.pairingNote: Pooled pair-quarters within country (equal weight per quarter×category).
